referents.why: Third masculine singular 'his' (loving devotion). Of the candidates, only the LORD (w2) is a masculine singular person who can own a devotion; w7 (forever) and w8 (the devotion itself) cannot. The LORD is the one thanked in cl0 and the one whose goodness and devotion cl1 and cl2 state.
referents.category: possessive pronoun, nearest agreeing named owner

referents.why: The command 'give thanks' has an implied second masculine plural 'you', the people it is spoken to. No candidate is a plural audience: w2 is the one thanked, not the one addressed; the writing and the psalmist voice are singular or not persons addressed. The verse does not name the audience.
referents.category: implied plural addressee of a command

links.why: The conjunction 'for' after the imperative gives the reason for giving thanks: He is good.
The second 'for' gives the ground of the claim that He is good: his loving devotion endures forever. The semicolon joins it as its reason, not as a separate assertion.

groups.why: The builder gave cl1 the role 'part', which the imperative kind does not have. The clause introduced by 'for' is the basis given for the command; the command is cl0.
groups.category: member role outside the group kind

groups.why: The verse opens the psalm and carries no heading, so there is no frame; the three clauses are what the psalm says. The builder named the LORD (w2) as sender, but the text does not name the writer: the LORD is the one thanked, not the one writing. The psalm's voice is a candidate, but the verse names no writer, so no sender is recorded.
groups.category: writing with no heading and no named writer

none_fit.what: The psalm's own voice is a candidate (voice), but the writing kind takes sender only where the text names the writer. A psalm whose verse names no writer has an unnamed voice with no slot to record it.

cant_tell.what: The audience of the command 'give thanks' (cl0s)
cant_tell.why: The imperative is plural and the verse does not say who is called to give thanks; the passage gives no wider context to settle it.
The verse does not name the writer, and its voice is not marked by any first-person form.
